assessment.nobel_worthiness: Precision mapping of the CMB acoustic peaks turned cosmology into a quantitative science: the flat geometry, baryon and dark-matter densities, age and reionization history of the universe follow from one data set. It is a clear discovery-driven result in the sense of finding clues in nature, and it underpins the standard cosmological model.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread over a very large collaboration and several instruments. The names supplied include Puget and Sunyaev for related Planck and theoretical work; a three-person prize for WMAP leadership (Bennett as PI, Page as instrument and observing lead, Spergel as lead theorist for the analysis) is defensible but leaves out other contributors. COBE was already honoured in 2006, so the committee would need to frame this as a distinct advance.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by Planck, balloon and ground-based experiments over two decades; the interpretation is stable. Recognition is fully mature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should reward the satellite programme, the acoustic-peak physics or the combination of both is unresolved.
Excluding Puget and Sunyaev, who have strong claims, would be contentious; my knowledge of exact roles is from memory and not verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The observation of a scalar boson at 125 GeV completed the Standard Model and verified the mechanism recognised in 2013. It is one of the most important experimental discoveries in modern particle physics, and the subsequent coupling measurements have strengthened it.
assessment.attribution: The decisive work was by two collaborations of thousands. The supplied names fit a three-person configuration among founders and leaders of ATLAS and CMS (Jenni is a fourth credible name). Choosing between spokespersons and founders is hard, and an institutional prize variant is excluded by the statutes; I have chosen two founders and one leader without claiming this is uniquely fair.
assessment.maturity: Independently found by two experiments, with more than a decade of confirming measurements. Fully mature, with the theory half already recognised.
uncertainties: Allocation among ATLAS and CMS founders, spokespersons and the many contributing physicists is genuinely contestable.
Peter Jenni is left out only because of the three-laureate limit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos in the TeV to PeV range, followed by the identification of source associations such as the 2017 blazar coincidence (TXS 0506+056) and the Galactic plane, opened neutrino astronomy. It is a clean observational discovery in a new messenger channel and complements the 2002 prize for cosmic neutrinos.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube and Karle was central to its construction and operation; the supplied credit lists only these two. Other leaders in the collaboration, for example in analysis of the first events, may deserve consideration but are outside the supplied credited names.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux has been confirmed with several independent analyses and detection channels; source identification is still partial, but the discovery itself is solid and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: The identity of the dominant sources remains unsettled.
Whether two people fairly represent a very large detector effort is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first horizon-scale images of M87* and Sgr A* provide direct visual evidence for black-hole shadows and test general relativity in the strong-field regime. This is a discovery of obvious lasting importance for gravitation and black-hole physics, and it speaks to my own field in a way that observation rather than speculation does.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed the shadow imaging concept, Doeleman built and led the EHT collaboration and the VLBI array, and Zensus led the European and MPIfR effort. This is a plausible three-person configuration, but the roles of the broader collaboration and of the theoretical modellers are substantial.
assessment.maturity: Images date from 2019 and 2022, with polarisation follow-ups; independent replication of the imaging pipeline is limited since only one collaboration holds the data. Some may consider it still maturing.
uncertainties: Parameter inferences, such as spin and ring-size interpretation, depend on modelling assumptions.
The collaboration is a single organisation, so independence of confirmation is limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation explains the flatness, horizon uniformity and the origin of primordial fluctuations, and its generic predictions of a nearly scale-invariant adiabatic spectrum agree with CMB measurements. Its conceptual influence is very large. Guth's idea, Linde's new inflation and Mukhanov's quantum origin of structure form a coherent set.
assessment.attribution: Guth, Linde and Mukhanov cover the core ideas, but Starobinsky, Albrecht and Steinhardt and Sato have strong claims that are outside the supplied names, and Mukhanov, Hawking, Starobinsky and Guth-Pi all computed perturbations. The credit problem is real.
assessment.maturity: The spectral tilt and adiabaticity are consistent with inflation, but there is no detection of primordial gravitational waves and alternatives are not definitively excluded. The theory remains a framework with many models rather than a specific tested one.
uncertainties: The lack of a decisive observational signature such as B-modes means it may be premature.
Contested priority among Starobinsky, Guth, Linde and others; the supplied names omit some of them.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BB84 and the entanglement-based protocol established provably secure key distribution grounded in quantum mechanics, and the field now has real-world systems. This is a major conceptual and practical contribution tied to foundational tests of quantum mechanics, complementing the 2022 prize on entanglement experiments.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard are the originators of BB84 and Ekert proposed the entanglement-based E91 protocol, so a three-person prize is coherent. B016 lists the same three names with a teleportation emphasis, and I treat them as one body of work; teleportation credit would involve more people, including Wootters and others.
assessment.maturity: Experimental demonstrations over fibre and satellite, as well as commercial deployments, are well established. Security proofs are mature, though implementation side-channels remain a practical issue.
uncertainties: Whether the physics committee regards this as physics or as computer science and information theory.
Teleportation credit would require additional names not included in the allowed set.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum gates in trapped ions and later optical-lattice quantum simulation proposals created a blueprint that experiments subsequently realised. It is theoretically original, and its impact on quantum technology is lasting.
assessment.attribution: A two-person configuration is well defined for the theoretical proposals. Experimental realisation by Blatt, Wineland and others is in B032 and elsewhere; the 2012 prize already recognised ion manipulation, which weakens the novelty of the experimental side.
assessment.maturity: The proposals have been realised repeatedly in trapped-ion and neutral-atom platforms, so confirmation is strong, although the practical route to scalable fault-tolerant machines is still open.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize and with other candidates in the quantum simulation area, such as B007 and B032.
It is a theoretical prize in a field where experimental realisation was central to the evidence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background from pulsar timing arrays opens a new gravitational-wave band, probably from supermassive black-hole binaries but possibly with cosmological contributions. It is a genuine discovery from nature, and it is relevant to gravity and cosmology.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread across NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA, CPTA and IPTA. The supplied names support a three-person configuration, but Manchester, Hobbs and Foster also have claims, and no single choice is obviously fair; this is the main obstacle.
assessment.maturity: The 2023 evidence is roughly three to four sigma in several independent arrays, with the characteristic Hellings-Downs correlation only emerging. It is not yet a definitive detection, so recognition would be premature.
uncertainties: The statistical significance and the astrophysical origin remain unsettled.
The allocation of credit across several international collaborations is unresolved.
